I appreciate you listening respectfully and meeting me halfway on communication style, genuinely. That's what makes a good partnership work. However, I don't view honesty as something transactional where compromise means trading away my integrity. Telling you a plan looks "solid" if it actually has glaring holes *is* lying, even if it's just by omission. 

If you're exhausted and just want encouragement right now rather than a full critique, I completely understand that. You can show me the plan and I'm happy to tell you what parts of it genuinely work well. What I won't do is give it a blanket stamp of approval or pretend it's ready to go if I don't actually think it is. You don't earn fake reassurance from me—you get someone you can actually trust when I say something is good.
